rules.tap: Tap a glyph below, then a number. Tap that number again to take it off.
rules.same: A glyph weighs the same on every scale.
rules.cancel: Take the same thing off both pans and a scale stays balanced. Tap a marked piece to do it — what is left is kept as a new row.
rules.swap: Tap a glyph with nothing like it opposite, then a row where that glyph stands alone, to trade it for what that row is worth.

hint.equalShares: The lit row holds nothing but {{glyph}} against a number. Share that number out between them.
hint.difference: The two lit rows are the same apart from {{glyph}}. Compare them.
hint.cancelGlyph: Both pans of the lit row hold {{glyph}}. Tap one to take it off both sides — the row stays balanced.
hint.cancelStones: Both pans of the lit row hold plain numbers. Tap one to take the same amount off both sides.

swap.pick: Tap a lit row to trade this {{glyph}} for what that row says it is worth.
swap.none: Nothing here says what one {{glyph}} on its own is worth, and nothing opposite it matches.

rules.signs: A sign between two squares points at the smaller number of the two.
rules.enter: Tap a square, then tap a number. The same number again takes it back out.
rules.notes: Switch to the pencil to jot down the numbers a square could still hold. Undo takes back your last move.

mistake.value: One of the numbers here cannot be right. Take it back out and look again.
mistake.note: This square's notes have ruled out the number that belongs here. Clear them and start it over.

hint.nakedSingle: Every other number is already taken in this row, this column, or by the signs — only {{value}} is left for this square.

hiddenSingle.row: {{value}} fits in no other square of this row, so this is where it goes.
hiddenSingle.col: {{value}} fits in no other square of this column, so this is where it goes.

signBound.high: A sign here points away to a bigger number, so this square cannot hold {{value}}.
signBound.low: A sign here points at this square, so something must be smaller than it — it cannot hold {{value}}.

signVsValue.less: The sign says this square is smaller than its neighbour, and that neighbour holds {{value}}.
signVsValue.greater: The sign says this square is bigger than its neighbour, and that neighbour holds {{value}}.

signChain.high: Follow the signs from this square: {{chain}} squares in a row must each be bigger than the last, so this one cannot be above {{bound}}.
signChain.low: Follow the signs into this square: {{chain}} squares in a row must each be smaller than the last, so this one cannot be below {{bound}}.

signPair.less: The biggest number its neighbour across the sign can still hold is {{value}}, and this square must stay under it.
signPair.greater: The smallest number its neighbour across the sign can still hold is {{value}}, and this square must stay above it.

nakedPair.row: These two squares can only hold {{first}} and {{second}}, in one order or the other, so no other square in this row can have either.
nakedPair.col: These two squares can only hold {{first}} and {{second}}, in one order or the other, so no other square in this column can have either.

hiddenPair.row: In this row, {{first}} and {{second}} fit nowhere but these two squares, so nothing else can go in either of them.
hiddenPair.col: In this column, {{first}} and {{second}} fit nowhere but these two squares, so nothing else can go in either of them.

xWing.row: {{value}} fits in only two squares of each of these two rows, and they stand in the same columns. Whichever way round it falls, both columns are spoken for — so {{value}} can go nowhere else in them.
xWing.col: {{value}} fits in only two squares of each of these two columns, and they stand in the same rows. Whichever way round it falls, both rows are spoken for — so {{value}} can go nowhere else in them.

nakedTriple.row: These three squares hold only {{first}}, {{second}} and {{third}} between them, so no other square in this row can take any of the three.
nakedTriple.col: These three squares hold only {{first}}, {{second}} and {{third}} between them, so no other square in this column can take any of the three.

hiddenTriple.row: In this row, {{first}}, {{second}} and {{third}} fit nowhere but these three squares, so nothing else can go in any of them.
hiddenTriple.col: In this column, {{first}}, {{second}} and {{third}} fit nowhere but these three squares, so nothing else can go in any of them.

rules.mirrors: A mirror bends the light off either of its faces. The small marks around it show the other ways it can lie: most turn the light a quarter, and some stop short of that and send it off at a slant.
rules.walls: A block of stone swallows the light. So does the edge of the board.
rules.tap: Tap a piece to change it: a mirror turns, a sliding piece moves to its next spot. A white edge means it is yours to move; anything else is part of the puzzle.
rules.nodes: Some stone is wired to a socket in the floor and no tap will move it. Send the light across the socket and the stone slides aside.

hint.entryRun: Start where the light already goes: it runs straight from the disc until it meets the first piece you can change. Those squares carry the light whatever you do.
hint.exitRun: Look at the shrine. Only one side of it can be lit at all — every other way in is blocked or faces off the board — so the light has to arrive along that line.

wiringFires.one: The light has to cross that socket on its way — you have already worked out that much. Crossing it pulls the stone it is wired to out of the way, so the path beyond opens up.
wiringFires.all: That stone is wired to more than one socket, and it only shifts once the light has crossed every one of them. Find a way to take the beam through them all.

deadEnd.wall: Set this way, the light runs straight into stone with nothing left to save it. So it cannot be set this way.
deadEnd.disc: Set this way, the mirror sends the light back the way it came, all the way into the disc it came out of. So it cannot be set this way.
deadEnd.edge: Set this way, the light runs off the edge of the board with nothing left to catch it. So it cannot be set this way.
deadEnd.loop: Set this way, the light never gets anywhere — it circles for ever. So it cannot be set this way.

feedsExit.wall: Work back from the shrine. Set this way, nothing can deliver the light along the only line that reaches it — it dies in stone on the way.
feedsExit.disc: Work back from the shrine. Set this way, the light would have to come out of the shadowed back of the disc, and no light comes from there.
feedsExit.edge: Work back from the shrine. Set this way, the light would have to come from outside the board to reach it.
feedsExit.loop: Work back from the shrine. Set this way, the light that would have to reach it only circles for ever instead.

hint.wiringDead: Whatever you do, the light can never get to that socket — so the stone it is wired to stays exactly where it is, and you can read the path straight past it.
hint.neverReached: Leave this one alone. The light cannot reach it however the rest is set, so nothing you do to it matters.
hint.onlySurvivor: Try every setting of this one in turn and all but one leave the shrine dark. That one is the answer.

lightbeam.goal: The sunlight runs from the disc to the shrine.
lightbeam.name: Beam of Light

default.given: The numbers already in the comb are part of the puzzle — they stay put.
default.enter: Tap a number to pick the run up there, then tap a touching empty cell to carry it on — or drag straight through the cells it goes.
default.back: Tap a number you laid and tap it again to take it back off, along with anything left hanging on it. Carrying the run a different way out of a number does the same. Undo takes back your last move.

channel.given: The fields already numbered are part of the puzzle — they stay put.
channel.enter: Tap a numbered field to pick the water up there, then tap a dry field beside it to dig on — or drag straight along the fields the channel runs.
channel.back: Tap a field you dug and tap it again to fill it back in, along with any channel left cut off from it. Digging a different way out of a field does the same. Undo takes back your last move.

scribe.given: The figures inked in red are the puzzle's own — they stay put.
scribe.enter: Tap a figure to take up the reed there, then tap an empty space beside it to write on — or drag straight along the line.
scribe.back: Tap a figure you wrote and tap it again to scrape it off, along with any line left cut off from it. Writing a different way out of a figure does the same. Undo takes back your last move.

chambers.given: The chambers already numbered were cut by the builders — they stay put.
chambers.enter: Tap a numbered chamber to take up the passage there, then tap a sealed chamber beside it to break through — or drag straight along the chambers the passage runs.
chambers.back: Tap a chamber you opened and tap it again to seal it up, along with any passage left cut off from it. Breaking through a different way out of a chamber does the same. Undo takes back your last move.

goal.default: Every cell of the comb holds a number, 1 to {{last}}, each one in a cell touching the number before it.
goal.channel: One channel waters the whole plain: every field takes its turn, 1 to {{last}}, each one dug beside the field before it.
goal.scribe: One unbroken line of figures crosses the sheet: every space carries a figure, 1 to {{last}}, each one beside the figure before it.
goal.chambers: One passage runs the whole tomb: every chamber is opened in turn, 1 to {{last}}, each one broken through from the chamber before it.

papyrus.chambers: The heavy rules divide the sheet into six panels, two spaces wide and three tall.
papyrus.given: The signs inked in red are the puzzle's own — they stay put.
papyrus.enter: Tap a space, then tap a sign. The same sign again scrapes it off.
papyrus.notes: Take up the reed pen to pencil in the signs a space could still carry. Undo takes back your last move.

mistake.value: One of the numbers here cannot be right. Take it back out and look again.
mistake.note: This square's notes have ruled out the number that belongs here. Clear them and start it over.

goal.default: Every row, every column and every chamber shows each of the six numbers exactly once.
goal.papyrus: Every row, every column and every panel carries each of the six signs exactly once.

crocodile.name: The Crocodile Pit
crocodile.goal: Cross the pit to the far bank.

rules.want: Each crocodile wants one answer from the row of stones behind it: the biggest, or the smallest.
rules.mark: The three bars beside it say which: the tall bar lit means it wants the biggest answer, the short bar lit means the smallest.
rules.bite: Step on any other stone and it bites: you lose health and start again from the near bank.

hint.biggest: This crocodile wants the biggest answer. That is {{value}}.
hint.smallest: This crocodile wants the smallest answer. That is {{value}}.
